newsitem.title: USA: Meredith to buy Connecticut TV station.
newsitem.headline: Meredith to buy Connecticut TV station.

text.p: Meredith Corp said Monday it agreed to acquire WFSB-TV, the CBS affiliate serving Hartford-New Haven, Conn., in exchange for WCPX-TV, the CBS affiliate serving Orlando, Fla.
The Florida station is among the properties Meredith agreed to purchase from First Media Television LP earlier this year.
Terms of the agreement to acquire WFSB from Post-Newsweek Stations Inc, a wholly owned subsidiary of Washington Post Co, call for an exchange of assets plus a $60 million cash payment to Meredith.

"As the top-rated station in the 27th largest market, WFSB fits nicely into our stated growth strategy to acquire network affiliated stations in the top 40 markets," William Kerr, Meredith president, said in a statement.
He added the deal also expands Meredith's reach to a growing market in the Northeast.
Meredith said the Hartford-New Haven designated market area has the fourth highest household income level and the third highest per capita income level among the top 40 markets in the country.
It added that broadcast industry analysts expect the annual market revenue to grow somewhat above the national average of five percent.

Meredith said the First Media deal included WCPX in Orlando, where it already owns Fox affiliate WOFL-TV. Because U.S. Federal Communications Commissions (FCC) regulations prohibit one company from owning two TV stations that serve the same viewing area, the latest deal resolves any ownership conflict it has in Orlando, Meredith added.
Meredith said its acquisition of WFSB is expected to close this fall, pending approval from the FCC. Purchase of three other stations from First Media is set to close this summer.
After crediting the $60 million cash payment in the WFSB-WCPX deal, the net cost to Meredith for the combined transaction is $375 million, or a multiple of 10 times cash flow.
Meredith said it will finance the acquisition through a combination of cash and debt.

When the acquisitions are complete, Meredith Broadcasting Group will include 11 stations. Meredith's other businesses include magazine and book publishing, residential real estate marketing and franchising, and brand licensing.
